questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: University of Manchester has a wide range of courses in Critical International Political Economy compared to other universities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Information about courses and locations were easy to find. However, it was difficult and stressfull to find housing, since the university didn't answer my housing applicatino.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I talked to the International Student Society, who guided my on how to get my Student ID card

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It would have been nice to have an introductory meeting with other Erasmus-students

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult and stressfull. I spend a week looking for housing, while living at an expensive hostel.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it's good idea to contact the unversity's accomodation service long time in advance, to be sure of having a place to stay

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy process. The course-coordinator was quick at answering questions about the available courses

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Easy contact to course-coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the clases I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact course-administrator to be sure about which courses are available.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were taught by mostly qualified lecturers. However, the level of the teaching was sometimes to low compared to what i'm use to. Instead of elaborating the difficult aspects of curriculum, the lectures sometimes only presented the main points which were easy to understand.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More student-integration. More seminar-based teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLI60032 Comparing Capitalisms in the Global Political Economy
POLI60182 Governing in an Unjust World
POLI70282 Critical Globalisation Studies
POLI70422 Global Governence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The lecturer in Comparing Capitalisms in the Global Political Economy was extreemly competent.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of sports acitivities and university societies. Strong international community.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Engaging in the student associations are a great way of getting to know people! I played badminton and went for board-game nights.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Peak District! Really beautifull area only 30 minutes by train outside of Manchester. Great for hiking

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Engage in student societies! Talk to people in your class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: British people spend a lot of time talking about drugs

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very friendly and open fellow students

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Choose Manchester if you are interested in more critical political science. Many courses are based on marxism, feminism, postcolinalism ec. 
2. Don't choose Manchester for the sake of the city's beauty. It's quite ugly, but also has its own charm and is very lively. 
3. Start finding housing early.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use facebook pages to find housing!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Interesting courses not avaialbe to me in DK!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
